messages:
IncidentBot: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected for service=redwood-inference, pool=shared-gpu-pool-3, metric=p99_latency_ms=2400ms (threshold=1500ms). Streaming stall rate up. Paging oncall: @Maria (oncall). Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/latency/shared-gpu-pool-3

Maria (oncall): ack. I'm on it. grabbing metrics and checking which tenants are spiking.

Jon SRE: I can repro tail at the host layer. gpu-3-17 and gpu-3-18 showing io_wait spikes and nvme latencies. p95 also drifting up.

Tara Eng: any cgroup OOM/kick events? cgroup throttling could explain progressive stalls in streaming.

Lee ML: model variants? are we falling back to a larger model that increases token generation time?

Maria (oncall): running quick host checks, grabbing iostat and dmesg. toggling stream samples off for a few tenants if needed.

Maria (oncall): results:
```
# iostat -x 1 3
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s rrqm/s wrqm/s  r_await  w_await  aqu-sz  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         1200.0  850.0  102400  204800    0.00   10.00    4.32   62.10   2.30   0.30  98.50
nvme1n1           30.0   20.0    5120    4096    0.00    0.00   12.10   10.40   0.05   0.40   2.00
```
nvme0n1 on gpu-3-17 is saturated. also seeing cgroup blkio.weight drops for tenant ten-0x4.

Jon SRE: exact. blkio throttle events logged at kernel: 
```
kernel: blkio: cgroup blkio.weight limit reached for group /kubepods.slice/.../ten-0x4
```
we're getting writeback congestion from that tenant.

Priya (CS): VIP customers 8472 and 9121 reported streaming stalls ~16:05 UTC, intermittent partial responses. Are we exposing impact on status page?

Maria (oncall): yes, customers impacted. Marking page status to "degraded performance". tagging Priya for downstream comms.

Tara Eng: short-term mitigation options: 1) evict the noisy tenant from shared pool, 2) throttle tenant IO/cpu via cgroup, 3) move heavy traffic to dedicated pool or fallback model.

Maria (oncall): I'm going to attempt an eviction for the top noisy tenant (ten-0x4) from shared-gpu-pool-3. running playbook now:
```
# runbook: evict noisy tenant
POST /ops/evict
payload: {"pool":"shared-gpu-pool-3","tenant":"ten-0x4","reason":"io-saturation"}
```

IncidentBot: Action recorded: evict job started (job_id=evict-3367894321-01). ETA ~ 90s.

Jon SRE: while eviction runs, I can apply blkio throttling to reduce writeback bursts:
```
echo 200 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/kubepods/.../ten-0x4/blkio.weight
```
set it to 200 from 1000 to limit bandwidth.

Maria (oncall): eviction completed. job evict-3367894321-01 succeeded. tenant ten-0x4 moved to isolation-queue. observing metrics...

Jon SRE: p99 dropped from 2400ms -> 800ms on the affected pool, p95 now 220ms. still seeing occasional streaming stalls but much less frequent.

Lee ML: can we switch affected customers to the cpu-fallback variant temporarily? less parallel token throughput but more predictable. we should roll traffic to model-variant:rw-fallback-v2.

Maria (oncall): initiating traffic reroute for customers flagged by CS (8472,9121) to fallback variant.

PagerDuty: Escalation: If p99 > 1000ms for > 10 minutes, escalate to infra-lead. current p99=780ms, monitoring.

Priya (CS): confirmed 8472 says streaming resumed but with slight lag. they appreciate the heads-up. can you provide ETA for full recovery?

Tara Eng: recommend leaving eviction + blkio throttling in place until nightly traffic drop, then schedule migration of top noisy tenants to dedicated pools or apply long-term QoS policies: per-tenant io.weight and writeback limits.

Maria (oncall): agreed. adding mitigation notes to the ticket INC-5421. Steps taken: eviction (ten-0x4), blkio weight reduced, traffic routed to fallback model for two customers, status page updated.

Jon SRE: follow-up investigation items: collect nvme SMART for gpu-3-17, check tenant pattern (burst vs sustained), identify any pod-level writeback spikes from model cache writes. I'll open a follow-up CR.

Lee ML: also add model cache sharding limits - large model downloads and checkpoint writes can saturate disk during warm starts. we should limit concurrent downloads per host.

Maria (oncall): oncall handoff scheduled. I'll remain in thread for 10m then hand off to Jon for next shift. current timestamps: 16:10 UTC - mitigation stable, p99=760ms.

Jon SRE: taking over monitoring. I'll coordinate a planned migration for the noisy tenant to dedicated capacity @ tomorrow 01:00 UTC.

Priya (CS): updating customers: "We identified a noisy tenant causing disk IO saturation in a shared GPU pool. We've isolated the tenant and applied mitigations; streaming should be stable now. We'll follow up with a permanent fix." :thumbsup:

Maria (oncall): handing off now to @Jon SRE. leaving runbook entry and logs in INC-5421. thanks team. :white_check_mark:

Jon SRE: ack, I have the ticket. I'll run postmortem template and include recommended QoS controls, eviction criteria, and a playbook step to proactively detect incoming writeback bursts.

IncidentBot: Thread closed for active paging. Please reopen if p99 > 1000ms or additional customer impact reported.
